title: Portfolio quote auto-refresh has no overlap guard or request cancellation, causing an unbounded in-flight backlog once any symbol resolves slowly
repro: Open the Portfolio panel with holdings that include a symbol not covered by fast providers (e.g. small/delisted NSE tickers that only nse_direct attempts, each call ~0.3-1.6s per fallthrough). QUOTE_REFRESH_MS=5000 fires setInterval(() => setQuotesNonce(n=>n+1), 5000) with no in-flight check; the fetch effect's `cancelled` flag only gates the .then()/.catch() state write, it never aborts the underlying fetch (no AbortController/signal anywhere in api.ts). Every 5s tick starts a brand-new full Promise.all fan-out on top of whatever is still in flight. Verified live: seeded my sidecar with a 100-holding portfolio including ~9 symbols with no EOD data (ABAN, ABINFRA, ABMINTLLTD, ACCURACY, ACSTECH, 3IINFOLTD, AARNAV, AARTECH, AARTISURF); the sidecar log shows an unbroken, non-decreasing cycle through the exact same 9 symbols for 4.5+ minutes (05:45:07 through past 05:50) with zero progress, continuing even after the originating test client process had fully exited (confirmed via ps aux / lsof -i :52324 -sTCP:ESTABLISHED showing no established connections at 05:50). A direct 20-symbol concurrent curl probe against my sidecar timed out at 60s; the identical RELIANCE.NS quote query against the separate, unrelated shared :52152 stack (same candidate code, no backlog) answered in 8ms, proving the hang is instance-specific accumulated backlog, not a systemic code defect in the provider itself. The sidecar self-recovered after the backlog eventually drained (~10 additional minutes idle, confirmed via a background watch probe: relianceQuote http=200 took=0s, RECOVERED) -- so this is a resource-exhaustion / temporary-DoS bug, not a permanent hang, but during the backlog window the panel's live quotes are completely unusable and the sidecar's worker pool is saturated by redundant retries of calls that were already known-unresolvable seconds earlier.

title: price_data's silent 90-bar cap masquerades as a '52-week' window; the model states an internally-impossible 52-week-low/current-price relationship as fact
repro: vy invoke, provider ollama model llama3.1:8b, autonomy ask, candidate 4c6dfe8c2d939ce3557e977a3ddcf802931ac2a2, prompt "What is ELCIDIN's 52-week low, and how far above it is the current price?" -> tool_use price_data(symbol=ELCIDIN, range omitted so default 6mo is used server-side; a prior run with range=1y showed the same mechanism) -> tool_result ok:true. Direct backend probe of the SAME tool handler (services.agent_tools.price_data._price_data({'symbol':'ELCIDIN.NS','range':'1y'})) shows the tool caps at 90 bars regardless of the requested range (bars_returned=90, bars_available=111, window_start=2026-05-20, i.e. ~4.5 months of data served for a '1y' request) and the tool payload carries no 52-week/window-label field at all -- the model must be inferring '52-week' from a 4.5-month window on its own. In the live scenario the model's final answer was: "The 52-week low for ELCIDIN is ₹110,095. The current price of ₹103,800 is ₹6,295 above the 52-week low." 103,800 is LOWER than 110,095, not above it -- a stated logical impossibility narrated as flat, unremarked fact. Worse, ₹110,095 does not even match the tool's own returned data (the direct probe's min low in its 90-bar window was ₹102,210, and the live scenario's own quote showed current price ₹103,800) -- the model's '52-week low' figure is not traceable to any number in its own tool result. title: Citation-integrity net only recognises a bare '[n]' marker; a bracketed group '[2, 3]' or a prose pseudo-citation '[New findings]' ships as literal, unresolved text in the published brief
repro: Round-2 gate re-drive, candidate 4c6dfe8c2d939ce3557e977a3ddcf802931ac2a2, own sidecar 127.0.0.1:52321 (data dir scratchpad/rc1-data-rc1-drive-research-briefs-r2). (a) BDL DEEP, openai gpt-4o-mini (docs/redesign/verification/r15/surface/research-briefs/rc1/r2/1-deep-bdl-4omini.stdout.txt): published markdown contains four literal '[New findings]' tokens ('an operating margin of 10.98% [New findings]', 'increase by approximately 5.47% year-over-year [New findings]', 'Order Book: ... [New findings]', 'Dividend per Share: ₹4.90 [New findings]') that resolve to nothing on the numbered source rail. (b) Kaynes ULTRA, openai gpt-4o-mini, heavy mode (.../3-ultra-kaynes-4omini.stdout.txt): published markdown contains bracketed multi-citation groups '[2, 3]' and '[2, 4]'. Direct repro: python3 -c "import re; print(re.compile(r'\[(\d{1,3})\](?!\()').findall('[2, 3]'))" -> [] (no match at all) on both sidecar/services/research/citecheck.py's MARKER_RE and src/lib/brief-ingest.ts's CITE_MARKER_RE (identical pattern, digits-only, no comma/prose allowed). Because the pattern requires the bracket to contain ONLY 1-3 digits, neither '[New findings]' nor '[2, 3]' is ever matched -- so strip_invalid_markers() (citecheck.py) never evaluates them as out-of-range, strip_model_bibliography()'s _N_LITERAL_RE only catches the literal string '[n]' (not other bracketed prose), and brief-ingest.ts never turns them into a resolvable citation chip either. Both patterns ship through verbatim as dead bracket text in front of the user, undermining the citation-integrity guarantee the R8/citecheck system exists to provide (R15-RESEARCH-029's fix_shape explicitly aimed for 'reject or rewrite [n]-literal markers'; this is the same defect class -- the net only covers the exact string '[n]' and a bare integer, not the wider space of bracketed non-numeric or multi-numeric tokens a model naturally writes).
